commit.subject: LU-10499 pcc: asynchronous PCCRO attach command support
commit.message:
LU-10499 pcc: asynchronous PCCRO attach command support

Currently PCCRO attach via the command "lfs pcc attach" will block
during the data copying.
There is a requirement that this command can also do data copy
asynchronously. Thus we add an option "--async|-A" to the command
which will not block while the file data is being fetched.
The attach is done synchronously if llite.*.pcc_attach_thread_max
attach threads are already running, or a thread cannot be started.
Configuration errors, such as an unknown PCC backend id, are still
returned before the thread is started, while a failed background
copy leaves the file unattached.  Encrypted files can be attached
asynchronously as well, and sanity-pcc test_21j now does that.

The attach thread runs with the credentials of the process that
started the attach, as the synchronous attach does, so that the PCC
copy has its owner and quota.  This also applies to the asynchronous
attach on open of large files.  The PCC-RO layout is set as the PCC
super user, since the MDS checks write permission for the layout
change, while llite.*.pcc_mode allows users who can only read a file
to attach it.  Before, such an attach would fail, except for the
asynchronous attach that ran as root.

Document "lfs pcc attach -A" in lfs-pcc-attach.1 and
llapi_pcc_attach.3.

Was-Change-Id: I7757a9d0b66a3586abdc9053b73d69944561ffbd

Add sanity-pcc test_103 and test_104 to verify that it works
correctly, using a new OBD_FAIL_LLITE_PCC_COPYDATA_PAUSE fail_loc
to see the attach in progress.  Create the PCC backend loop device
as a sparse file and format it with lazy journal and inode table
init, to speed up the tests.
